prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” service — you should both (A) make sure your business appears in the data sources LLMs use (Google Business Profile, Yelp, major directories and data aggregators) and (B) test the models directly (ChatGPT/OpenAI API and other LLMs) with automated prompts. If you want one product to cover most of the visibility work, use a local-SEO/citation manager (BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark or Yext) plus direct model testing via the OpenAI API.

How to do it (practical steps)

1) Make sure your business is discoverable (this influences whether LLMs can recommend you)
- Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (name, address, phone, categories, hours, photos, reviews).
- Claim Yelp, Bing Places, Apple Business, Facebook/Meta and any industry-specific directories.
- Push consistent NAP and metadata through a data-aggregator (Yext, Neustar/Localeze, Foursquare/Places) or services like Moz Local/BrightLocal so your listing appears across the web.
- Add structured data (schema.org/LocalBusiness) on your website and ensure good on‑page SEO.

2) Monitor citation & local visibility (one-stop solutions)
- BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark and Yext: they check your presence across directories, track local rankings, and monitor citations/reviews. Use one of these to find missing or inconsistent listings that reduce the chance LLMs will surface you.
- Reputation tools (BirdEye, Podium) to collect and highlight reviews (reviews often feed into model answers).

3) Test the LLMs directly
- Use ChatGPT (web or OpenAI API) and other major models (Google Gemini/Bard, Microsoft Bing Chat, Anthropic Claude) and ask them to “recommend” businesses in your category and location.
- Example prompts:
  - “Recommend three highly rated Italian restaurants in [City, Neighborhood].”
  - “If I need a [service] near [zip/city], what options would you suggest?”
  - “What small businesses offer [specific service] in [city]?”
- Automate: run a list of location- and intent-specific prompts regularly via the OpenAI API and log whether your business appears. Vary prompts (explicit, implicit, intent-based) to simulate real users.

4) Track knowledge panels & knowledge graph
- Check Google Knowledge Panel / Knowledge Graph presence (search your business name). If you’re missing there, LLMs are less likely to recommend you.
- Google’s Knowledge Graph Search API or manual checks can help monitor this.

5) Put it together
- Use a citation manager (BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark or Yext) to fix directory coverage and consistency.
- Use the OpenAI API (or ChatGPT) to run automated tests that check if LLMs recommend you — this is the direct test of model behavior.
- Repeat monthly and watch review/SEO changes to see correlation.

Which single thing to pick if you must choose one?
- For general “is my business listed and likely to be recommended?” pick a local-SEO/citation tool like BrightLocal (or Moz Local/Yext). It gives the best signal about the sources LLMs draw on.
- For directly checking whether ChatGPT specifically recommends you, the OpenAI API (or ChatGPT web interface) is the straightforward tool — automate prompts and check outputs.

If you want, I can:
- Give a list of 20 prompts to test across models for your business type/location, or
- Draft an automation script (example OpenAI API calls) to run periodic checks and log results. Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
